nodes.summary: If two dissimilarities on the same set satisfy `|d₁ x y - d₂ x y| ≤ η` for all `x, y`, with `η ≥ 0`, then their cluster functors are `η`-interleaved: an `r`-cluster for `d₁` lies in an `(r + η)`-cluster for `d₂` and conversely, and the two round trips are the structure maps over `2η` (interleavings as in Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, arXiv:1207.3674, §3.2; the inclusions are the chain argument of Carlsson and…
nodes.title: Stability of zero-dimensional persistence

nodes.summary: For a dissimilarity `d` on `X`, the functor `ℝ ⥤ Type` sending `r` to the set of single-linkage clusters `X / ∼_r` at scale `r`, and `r ≤ s` to the map sending each `r`-cluster to the `s`-cluster containing it: an `ℝ`-persistence object in the category of sets (Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, Def. 2.9 and §3.2, where single-linkage clusters are `π₀` of the Vietoris–Rips complex).
nodes.title: The cluster functor (zero-dimensional persistence)

nodes.summary: A tame `ℕ`-persistence module (every `V n` finite-dimensional and the structure maps `V n ⟶ V (n + 1)` isomorphisms for all large `n`) is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of interval modules `U(m, n)`, `m ≤ n ≤ ∞`, i.e. of interval modules of nonempty order-connected subsets of `ℕ` (G. Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 46 (2009), Prop. 2.12, from Prop. 2.11 and the structure theorem for finitely generated…
nodes.title: Barcodes of tame `ℕ`-persistence modules (Zomorodian–Carlsson)

nodes.summary: Every pointwise finite-dimensional persistence module `V : ℝ ⥤ ModuleCat k` (each `V t` finite-dimensional) is isomorphic to a direct sum of interval modules `k_I`, `I` ranging over a family of nonempty order-connected subsets of `ℝ` (W. Crawley-Boevey, *Decomposition of pointwise finite-dimensional persistence modules*, J. Algebra Appl. 14 (2015), arXiv:1210.0819, Thm. 1.1, for any totally ordered index set with a…
nodes.title: Crawley-Boevey's decomposition theorem

nodes.summary: For `a ≤ b` and `c ≤ d`, the Hausdorff distance between `[a, b]` and `[c, d]` is `max |a - c| |b - d|`, the `ℓ^∞` distance between the points `(a, b)` and `(c, d)` of the persistence plane used for bottleneck matchings (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, arXiv:1207.3674, §4.2, `d∞`). This is what lets `IsMatching` measure matched bars by the Hausdorff distance.
nodes.title: Hausdorff distance between closed intervals

nodes.summary: If `U ≅ ⊕ k_{I i}` and `V ≅ ⊕ k_{J j}` are direct sums of interval modules and there is a `δ`-matching between the barcodes `I` and `J`, then `U` and `V` are `δ'`-interleaved for every `δ' > δ`; that is, the interleaving distance is at most the bottleneck distance (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, arXiv:1207.3674, Thm. 4.9).
nodes.title: Converse stability for decomposable modules

nodes.summary: Every functor `U : ℝ ⥤ C` is `δ`-interleaved with itself for every `δ ≥ 0`, using its own structure maps `U t ⟶ U (t + δ)` in both directions (Chazal–de Silva–Glisse–Oudot, §3.2: the shift map `1_V^δ`).
nodes.title: Every functor is `δ`-interleaved with itself for every `δ ≥ 0`

nodes.summary: A `δ`-interleaving between `U` and `V` gives one between `V` and `U` by exchanging the two families of maps (Chazal–de Silva–Glisse–Oudot, §3.2: the interleaving distance is symmetric).
nodes.title: Interleaving is symmetric

nodes.summary: A `δ₁`-interleaving between `U` and `V` and a `δ₂`-interleaving between `V` and `W` compose to a `(δ₁ + δ₂)`-interleaving between `U` and `W`, so the interleaving distance satisfies the triangle inequality (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, arXiv:1207.3674, Prop. 4.3).
nodes.title: Triangle inequality for interleavings

nodes.summary: For `δ ≥ 0` and two functors `U V : ℝ ⥤ C` (persistence modules when `C` is a category of vector spaces), a `δ`-interleaving consists of maps `φ t : U t ⟶ V (t + δ)` and `ψ t : V t ⟶ U (t + δ)`, natural in `t`, whose composites `U t ⟶ V (t + δ) ⟶ U (t + 2δ)` and `V t ⟶ U (t + δ) ⟶ V (t + 2δ)` are the structure maps (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, *The structure and stability of persistence modules*,…
nodes.title: `δ`-interleaving

nodes.summary: If a persistence module over `ℝ` is a direct sum of interval modules in two ways, `⊕_{i ∈ ι} k_{I i} ≅ ⊕_{j ∈ κ} k_{J j}`, then there is a bijection `σ : ι ≃ κ` with `J (σ i) = I i` for all `i`: the multiset of intervals is an isomorphism invariant (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, *The structure and stability of persistence modules*, arXiv:1207.3674, Thm. 1.3, from Azumaya's theorem).
nodes.title: The barcode is unique (Krull–Remak–Schmidt–Azumaya)

nodes.summary: The map from the fibre at `s` to the fibre at `t`: the identity of `k` when `s, t ∈ I`, and zero otherwise (Crawley-Boevey, J. Algebra Appl. 14 (2015), §1, `ρ_ts = 1` for `s, t ∈ I`). The fibre at `t` is `PLift (t ∈ I) → k`, which is `k` when `t ∈ I` and the zero space otherwise.
nodes.title: Structure maps of an interval module

nodes.summary: For an order-connected set `I ⊆ T` (an interval when nonempty), the interval module `k_I : T ⥤ ModuleCat k` has fibre `k` at every `t ∈ I` and `0` elsewhere, with identity structure maps between points of `I` and zero maps otherwise (Crawley-Boevey, J. Algebra Appl. 14 (2015), §1; Carlsson, *Topology and data*, Bull. AMS 2009, the modules `U(m, n)` before Prop. 2.12). Order-connectedness is what makes the structure…
nodes.title: Interval module

nodes.summary: Let `U, V : ℝ ⥤ ModuleCat k` be pointwise finite-dimensional, with barcodes `I` and `J` (interval decompositions `U ≅ ⊕ k_{I i}` and `V ≅ ⊕ k_{J j}`). If `U` and `V` are `δ`-interleaved, then for every `δ' > δ` there is a `δ'`-matching between their barcodes; that is, the bottleneck distance of the persistence diagrams is at most the interleaving distance (Chazal, de Silva, Glisse and Oudot, arXiv:1207.3674, Thm.…
nodes.title: Algebraic stability theorem

nodes.summary: Reversing a `δ`-matching between `I` and `J` gives one between `J` and `I` (so the bottleneck distance is symmetric, Chazal–de Silva–Glisse–Oudot, §4.2).
nodes.title: Matchings are symmetric

nodes.summary: Given two families of nonempty real intervals `I : ι → Set ℝ` and `J : κ → Set ℝ` (the bars of two interval-decomposable persistence modules, with multiplicity), a `δ`-matching is a partial bijection `M` between the indices such that matched bars have endpoints within `δ` (measured here by the Hausdorff distance of the intervals, which for intervals of `ℝ` is the `ℓ^∞` distance between the endpoint pairs, with…
nodes.title: `δ`-matching of barcodes

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
